title: Delimex Brings Fresh, Authentic Mexican Street Flavors to the Frozen Aisle
summary: Delimex, a Kraft Heinz Company brand, is relaunching its frozen taquito line with refreshed packaging, enhanced flavor, and nearly double the filling, inspired by consumer insights into the $6 billion frozen snack category. To celebrate its Mexican heritage, Delimex has partnered with muralists Ale Ballesteros and Raul Urias to create murals in Dallas and Baltimore. The new products and branding are rolling out nationwide at major retailers.

title: Amazon Got a Big Boost During the Pandemic—And So Did Its Carbon Emissions
summary: Amazon's carbon footprint increased by 18% in 2021, reaching 71.54 million metric tons of carbon-dioxide equivalent, marking a 40% rise since 2019. This surge is attributed to the company's rapid growth during the pandemic, despite nascent efforts to reduce its environmental impact. While Amazon's carbon intensity fell, indicating improved efficiency in operations, achieving its net-zero goal by 2040 remains a significant challenge given its expansive business model.

title: Amid economic and stock volatility, Warren Buffett remains No. 3 investor in Kroger
summary: Legendary investor Warren Buffett maintains his position as Kroger's third-largest shareholder, holding over $3 billion in shares, despite current economic and stock market volatility. Buffett, known for his "value investing" approach, favors financially sound companies like Kroger that tend to perform steadily even during tough times. His continued investment is seen as a tacit endorsement, and Kroger's shares have shown resilience, being up double digits this year, following a significant jump after his initial investment disclosure in early 2020.

title: Here’s Why the Geovax Labs (GOVX) Stock Price Soared 63.4%
summary: Geovax Labs (GOVX) stock price surged 63.4% premarket after the company announced positive efficacy study results for its modified Ankara (MVA) vaccine against the Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV). This rally extended a 37% gain from the previous Friday, driven by a peer-reviewed animal study published in NPJ Vaccines. While the news is positive, the author warns against chasing the stock after such a significant rally, suggesting pullbacks often follow.

title: How Capital One improves visibility into Snowflake costs
summary: Capital One has launched Capital One Software, a new business selling its internal cloud cost management and governance tools, with its first product, Slingshot, targeting the Snowflake platform. This move allows Capital One to monetize its extensive cloud migration work and helps other enterprises manage Snowflake costs and automate governance, while also showcasing Snowflake's capabilities for highly regulated industries. Slingshot has already helped Capital One reduce Snowflake costs by 27%, improve cost per query by 45%, and save over 50,000 hours of work.

title: Cohesity names former VMware COO Sanjay Poonen as CEO
summary: Cohesity Inc., a data management provider, has appointed Sanjay Poonen, former COO of VMware Inc., as its new president and chief executive officer. Poonen replaces Cohesity founder Mohit Aron, who will transition to chief technology and product officer. This leadership change comes after Cohesity surpassed an annual revenue run rate of $300 million and boasts over 3,000 customers, including major financial institutions and Fortune 500 companies.

title: AEO’s Supply Chain Platform Cozies Up to DHL E-Commerce
summary: American Eagle Outfitters' subsidiary, Quiet Platforms, has partnered with DHL eCommerce Solutions to offer a new delivery service to retailers and brands within its network, including Peloton, Steve Madden, Li & Fung, and Fanatics. This collaboration aims to provide affordable last-mile services and date-definitive delivery across 93 percent of U.S. postal codes without custom integration. The move furthers Quiet Platforms' goal of democratizing the national carrier network and expanding its parcel delivery footprint.

title: Join our Microsoft Technologies Discipline
summary: EPAM is actively recruiting for its Microsoft Technologies Discipline, seeking over 3,500 .NET engineers, solution architects, and managers across more than 55 countries. The company highlights opportunities to work on innovative SaaS/PaaS cloud solutions, build CI/CD pipelines, and develop cloud-native applications for world-class clients, emphasizing professional growth and a strong AI community. EPAM showcases several projects, including those in oil and gas, IoT, life sciences research, and finance, applying technologies like .NET, Azure, Kubernetes, and GenAI.

title: Oracle Reportedly Initiating Layoffs in Bay Area, Other Locations
summary: Oracle has reportedly begun laying off thousands of employees in Silicon Valley and other global locations, targeting a billon dollars in expenses. These cuts occur despite strong profits and revenues, as Oracle is heavily investing in becoming a major cloud-services player to compete with Amazon Web Services, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud, while simultaneously continuing to pay specialized technologists competitive salaries. The company's strategy involves significant investment in cloud infrastructure while also reducing its workforce in other areas.

title: Semtech buys Sierra Wireless in $1.2bn deal ...
summary: Semtech has announced a definitive agreement to acquire wireless module maker Sierra Wireless for $1.2 billion, significantly expanding its market in cellular IoT modules and cloud services. The deal is expected to double Semtech's annual revenue and enhance its position in the Internet of Everything market by combining cellular, LoRa, and cloud services. This acquisition follows similar consolidation in the IoT sector and positions Semtech to offer multi-radio solutions and chip-to-cloud services.

title: Ulta Beauty Launches Digital Innovation Fund, Prisma Ventures
summary: Ulta Beauty has launched Prisma Ventures, a $20 million digital innovation fund aimed at investing in emerging technology startups. This initiative will focus on shaping future online and in-store experiences through enhanced discovery, personalization, and convenience, aligning with Ulta Beauty's digital innovation priorities in areas like AI, AR, VR, and social commerce. The fund offers not just capital but also access to Ulta Beauty's expertise, consumer insights, and in-market testing opportunities to foster strategic partnerships and accelerate retail and beauty innovation.

title: Arlo Pro 4 Spotlight vs. Ring Spotlight Camera: Which should you buy?
summary: This article compares two popular battery-powered outdoor security cameras, the Arlo Pro 4 Spotlight and the Ring Spotlight Camera, to help consumers decide which one best suits their smart home needs. It delves into their differences in video quality, spotlight brightness, smart features, smart home integrations, subscription costs, and battery life. Ultimately, the Arlo Pro 4 is recommended for its higher resolution camera and broader integration, while the Ring Spotlight Camera is highlighted for its brighter spotlight and longer video history, appealing particularly to those within the Alexa ecosystem.

title: Report: Company planning to build largest tower at The Domain
summary: Cousins Properties Inc. is planning to build a new 26-story office tower called Domain Central 1 at The Domain in Austin, Texas. This tower, which will include office space, retail, amenity floors, and parking, is projected to be the tallest and largest building in The Domain at an estimated cost of $143 million. The company also intends to redevelop existing office buildings in the area.

title: Etsy India appoints former Amazon executive Pankaj Jathar as VP, country head
summary: Etsy India has appointed Pankaj Jathar, a former Amazon executive and CEO of Prione, as its Vice President and Country Head for India operations. Jathar will be responsible for scaling Etsy's marketplace capabilities, identifying growth opportunities in India, and connecting local sellers with global buyers. Etsy considers India one of its seven core markets and has been investing in the country.

title: Microstrategy Outperforms Every Asset Class and Big Tech Stock Since Adopting Bitcoin Strategy, Says CEO
summary: Microstrategy CEO Michael Saylor highlights that the company's bitcoin strategy has led to significant outperformance against all asset classes and major tech stocks since its adoption. Saylor attributes this success to bitcoin's digital property characteristics and its appeal as a safe haven asset. The company's unique approach involved acquiring substantial bitcoin holdings and integrating it into their corporate strategy.

title: Waldencast (Nasdaq:WALD) - Stock Analysis
summary: This Simply Wall St report analyzes Waldencast (NASDAQ:WALD), a beauty and wellness company, highlighting its current stock performance, valuation, and financial health. The company is experiencing high share price volatility and unprofitability, with analysts trimming price targets due to sales shortfalls and higher costs. Recent developments include the conclusion of an SEC investigation and the acquisition of Novaestiq Corp. to expand into the dermal filler market.

title: Veritone Creates AI-Driven Revenue Opportunities for Enterprise Media & Entertainment Companies on AWS
summary: Veritone announced an extension of its collaboration with Amazon and AWS to support its Media & Entertainment (M&E) customers, leveraging its aiWARE platform to create AI-driven revenue opportunities. By integrating with AWS, Veritone's solutions help M&E companies modernize content production, management, and monetization, including processing vast amounts of media, creating metadata, and enabling Web3 activations. The collaboration aims to provide IP owners and content creators with tools to maximize revenue and engage audiences in increasingly immersive digital environments, as evidenced by clients like the San Francisco Giants and CBS News.

title: Atlas Air to Be Bought by Apollo-Led Group
summary: Atlas Air Worldwide Holdings Inc. has agreed to be acquired by a consortium of investors led by Apollo Global Management Inc. in an all-cash deal. The agreement values the freight aircraft operator at $3.2 billion in equity and approximately $5.2 billion in enterprise value. Shareholders will receive $102.50 per share, representing a 57% premium to the 30-day volume-weighted average trading price as of July 29.

title: A New Way to Connect Microsoft Teams with the Contact Centre
summary: This article discusses the growing need to integrate contact center capabilities with Microsoft Teams, especially for businesses seeking a unified platform for communications and customer service. It highlights the Voca Conversational Interaction Center by AudioCodes as a solution that offers "contact center lite" features and conversational AI, leveraging Microsoft's ecosystem. The piece also details three models for Teams contact center integrations (Connect, Extend, Power), with AudioCodes' Voca adopting the advanced "Power" model to enhance agent and customer experiences.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market Surpasses Expectations in Q2
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market reported strong second-quarter results, with net sales reaching $1.6 billion, a 5% increase year-over-year, and comparable-store sales growth of 2.0%. The healthy grocer's performance was attributed to disciplined execution of its long-term strategy, including new store openings and strategic partnerships like those with Pod Foods and Instacart for SNAP payments. Despite inflationary pressures, Sprouts remains cautiously optimistic and reaffirmed its full-year 2022 outlook, planning continued investment in new stores and capital expenditures.

title: Online Home Decor Market size to grow by USD 52.95 billion, Market Research insights highlight the rise in online spending and smartphone penetration as Key Driver - Technavio
summary: The online home decor market is projected to grow by USD 52.95 billion between 2021 and 2025, exhibiting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9%. This growth is primarily driven by increased online spending and smartphone penetration. Europe is expected to account for 42% of this market expansion, with key contributions from the UK and Germany.

title: Amazon.com Inc. – Cost pressures surpassing healthy demand
summary: Amazon's Q2 2022 revenue exceeded expectations, but earnings were negatively impacted by a significant pre-tax valuation loss from Rivian Automotive and substantial incremental costs due to inflation, including higher fuel and freight rates. In response to these pressures, the company is focusing on improving fulfillment efficiency and adjusting staffing levels, while maintaining a NEUTRAL rating and an unchanged target price of US$133.00 due to expected suppressed earnings in the near term. AWS continues to be a strong growth driver and a focus for investment, despite overall margin pressure.

title: Jeff Bezos’s Parents Buy two Miami Mansions
summary: Jeff Bezos's parents, Jackie and Mike Bezos, have purchased two luxury mansions in Miami. The primary residence is a 12,829-square-foot home bought for $34 million, featuring extensive amenities like a rock climbing wall and chef's kitchen. They also acquired an 8,713-square-foot "guest house" next door for $44 million, which boasts high-end materials and 500 feet of ocean frontage.

title: OKC, have a million drinks on Simple Modern, thanks to what CEO Mike Beckham sees in China
summary: Simple Modern, a company based in Moore, Oklahoma, led by co-founder Mike Beckham, is moving its drinkware and other product manufacturing from China to a new factory in south Oklahoma City. This move is part of a broader "reshoring" trend among U.S. manufacturers, driven by disruptions in the global supply chain due to the COVID-19 pandemic and geopolitical tensions. Simple Modern plans to invest $4-5 million in the plant, create over 100 jobs, and aims to produce millions of units of drinkware annually in Oklahoma, enhancing supply chain reliability and maintaining affordable prices.

title: Oracle lays off hundreds of employees
summary: Oracle has laid off hundreds of employees, primarily from its advertising and customer experience group, to prioritize its healthcare IT services and cloud businesses. This move comes after its recent $28.3 billion acquisition of Cerner Corp. and reflects a broader trend of tech companies making staffing adjustments amid an economic slowdown, shifting focus to high-priority areas like cloud infrastructure.

title: iRobot in Massachusetts: A timeline of the company's 32-year history.
summary: This article provides a timeline of iRobot's 32-year history in Massachusetts, noting Amazon's recent intent to acquire the company. It highlights iRobot (IRBT) as the latest Massachusetts tech firm to be acquired by Amazon, following Kiva Systems and PillPack. The piece serves as an introduction to a detailed history of the company.

title: Amazon to Buy Maker of the Roomba for $1.7 Billion (Published 2022)
summary: Amazon announced an agreement to acquire iRobot Corp., the maker of the Roomba robotic vacuum, for $1.7 billion. This acquisition adds to Amazon's expanding smart home product portfolio, which already includes Alexa and Ring doorbells. The deal, Amazon's fourth-largest recorded acquisition, highlights an ongoing trend of tech giants expanding their reach into automated home technologies and services.

title: Amazon’s iRobot Deal Seen Facing Tough FTC Antitrust Review
summary: Amazon's $1.65 billion acquisition of iRobot is expected to face a rigorous antitrust review from the US Federal Trade Commission (FTC), led by Chair Lina Khan. This scrutiny comes amidst Amazon's aggressive acquisition strategy and Khan's past criticisms of the e-commerce giant's market dominance, particularly concerning its potential to further dominate the smart home space. The FTC will also review Amazon's recent acquisition of One Medical.

title: Eli Lilly plans for growth in other states after Indiana passes near-total abortion ban
summary: Following Indiana's near-total abortion ban, pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly announced plans to seek employment growth outside its home state, citing concerns about attracting talent. The company, which is headquartered in Indianapolis, joined other major employers in committing to cover travel for reproductive services. This decision comes after Indiana became the first state to approve new abortion restrictions post-Roe v. Wade, a move also criticized by the Biden administration.

title: Better Buy: iShares S&P Core 500 Small Cap ETF or Vanguard S&P 500 ETF?
summary: This article compares the iShares S&P Core 500 Small Cap ETF (IJR) and the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO), discussing their features, risks, and benefits for investors. While VOO offers stability with large-cap companies, IJR provides potential for higher upside with small-cap stocks, albeit with increased volatility. The choice between them depends on an investor's strategy, risk tolerance, and investment goals.

title: Amazon is reportedly buying Roomba vaccum maker iRobot Corp.
summary: Amazon announced its acquisition of iRobot Corp., the maker of Roomba vacuums, for $1.65 billion. This move reinforces Amazon's push into internet-connected home devices and robotics, integrating iRobot's technology with its smart home ecosystem like Alexa and Echo speakers. The acquisition comes as iRobot faces waning demand post-pandemic and patent infringement battles, while Amazon continues its strategy of acquiring companies in hot or adjacent markets, following its recent bid for One Medical's parent company.

title: CVS plans bid for Dallas-based home health provider Signify Health
summary: CVS Health Corp. is reportedly planning to bid for Dallas-based Signify Health Inc. to expand into home-health services. This move aligns with CVS CEO Karen Lynch's strategy to increase direct patient care and compete with companies like Amazon, which recently acquired One Medical. Signify Health, which went public in 2021 and recently exited the bundled health insurance payments business to focus on home health, saw its shares rise by 40% this year and reported $773.4 million in revenue in 2021.

title: CloudGuard Spectral detects several malicious packages on PyPI - the official software repository for Python developers
summary: Check Point Research's CloudGuard Spectral detected 10 malicious packages on PyPI, the leading Python package index, which contained info-stealers designed to compromise developers' private data and credentials. These packages mimicked legitimate software or used deceptive descriptions to trick users, with cases like "Ascii2text" and "Pyg-utils" installing credential-harvesting scripts and connecting to malicious domains. CPR immediately reported these findings to PyPI, leading to the removal of the identified malicious packages, and urges developers to exercise caution given the increasing threat of supply chain attacks.

title: Putting the emphasis on IEC 62368-1 Overvoltage Compliance
summary: The article discusses the importance of complying with the IEC 62368-1 standard for electronic equipment, especially concerning overvoltage and overcurrent protection in universal power adapters. It highlights how this newer, hazard-based standard is more flexible and future-proof than its predecessors, requiring careful consideration of protection components like varistors, GDTs, and fuses. The authors, from Littelfuse, Inc., detail the scope, criteria, and testing functions required by IEC 62368-1, offering guidance on selecting appropriate protection components for reliable and safe electronic designs.

title: Gymboree, the iconic brand of The Children’s Place, launches on Amazon
summary: Gymboree, a brand under The Children's Place, has expanded its reach by launching on Amazon.com, offering its playful apparel to a broader customer base. This strategic move aims to leverage Amazon's platform for significant growth, complementing Gymboree's existing online presence and availability in over 100 Children's Place retail stores. Jane Elfers, president and CEO, highlighted the excitement about the collaboration and its potential for brand exposure.

title: iRobot and Its Roombas Could Give Amazon a Window Into Your Home
summary: Amazon's acquisition of iRobot for $1.7 billion raises concerns about user data privacy, specifically regarding the information Roombas gather about homes. The article suggests Amazon is interested in this data to enhance targeted advertising and potentially integrate iRobot's technology into its smart home ecosystem. It highlights how Roomba's mapping capabilities and object recognition, combined with Amazon's history of data utilization, could provide the tech giant with unprecedented insights into consumers' living spaces.

title: Cybersecurity skills shortage provides rare cross-training opportunities
summary: The article highlights the significant cybersecurity skills shortage in the U.S., presenting it as a unique opportunity for individuals to cross-train and enter a high-paying field. It discusses the attributes that make a good cybersecurity analyst, dispels the myth that a college degree is always required, and outlines various certification paths, including those for cloud security and zero trust frameworks, emphasizing the benefits for both individuals and global security.

title: Ex-JPMorgan CEO says highly successful people get outside their comfort zones: 'That's how you keep growing'
summary: Former JPMorgan Chase CEO Bill Harrison emphasizes that highly successful individuals consistently step outside their comfort zones to foster continuous growth. Harrison, who led JPMorgan from 2000 to 2006, shared his personal experiences, including an initial reluctance to move to London for a management role that ultimately became a pivotal learning experience. His advice is supported by recent psychological research indicating that embracing discomfort can lead to greater learning and personal development.

title: Cummins Inc. opposes Indiana’s near-total abortion ban
summary: Cummins Inc. has publicly opposed Indiana's new near-total abortion ban, stating it will make it difficult to attract talent and influence future growth decisions. The company, which employs over 10,000 people in Indiana, emphasized its commitment to providing employees with access to high-quality, affordable healthcare and reproductive health benefits. This opposition follows a similar stance from Eli Lilly and aligns with criticism from the Biden administration regarding the ban's impact.

title: 'Course Correct' This: Discovery Plus Surrenders Its App Experience to Yet Another Wholesale Partner, Sling TV
summary: Discovery Plus has partnered with Sling TV, allowing Sling users to sign up and watch Discovery Plus content directly through the Sling TV app. This move is part of Warner Bros. Discovery's strategy to reverse former WarnerMedia CEO Jason Kilar's approach of limiting wholesale partnerships and regain market share. The partnership is a significant shift back towards broader distribution channels, similar to previous deals with Amazon Prime Video Channels and Roku Channel, indicating a "course correction" by current WBD management.

title: Overtime Raises $100 Million in Series D Funding Round Led by Liberty Media Corporation and Counterpoint Global (Morgan Stanley)
summary: Overtime announced it has raised $100 million in Series D funding led by Liberty Media Corporation and Counterpoint Global (Morgan Stanley), bringing its total funding to over $250 million. The investment will fuel the expansion of its disruptive sports leagues, Overtime Elite (OTE) and OT7, and support the creation of new leagues, e-commerce, and web3 initiatives. Notable investors include Bezos Expeditions, Blackstone, and Sapphire Sport, reflecting confidence in Overtime's growth potential and its ability to engage Gen Z and Millennial sports communities.

title: Chuck Schumer’s Family Is Getting Nice Work on Wall Street
summary: The article highlights how Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer's family members and former staffers are being hired by major corporations like Blackstone, Amazon, Intel, and Google to lobby on legislation before the Senate. This raises concerns about potential conflicts of interest, especially regarding Schumer's role in advancing or delaying legislation that impacts these companies. Specifically, it details Blackstone's hiring of Schumer's son-in-law around the time a tax loophole benefiting private equity was being debated and Schumer's delay in bringing antitrust legislation against tech monopolies to a vote, given his daughters' employment by these tech giants.

title: Walmart Ponders Streaming Deal With Paramount, Disney and Comcast (Published 2022)
summary: Walmart is reportedly in discussions with major media companies, including Paramount, Disney, and Comcast, to integrate a streaming service into its Walmart+ membership program. This initiative aims to expand Walmart's relationship with customers beyond its physical stores, similar to how wireless providers have bundled streaming services. The move is seen as an effort to compete with Amazon.com's Prime and maintain its influence in the entertainment sector as consumption shifts online.

title: Overtime eyes more sports leagues after US$100m funding round led by F1 owner Liberty Media
summary: Digital sports media company Overtime has secured US$100 million in a Series D funding round, co-led by Formula One's commercial rights holder Liberty Media and Morgan Stanley's Counterpoint Global Fund. This investment, bringing Overtime's total funding to over US$250 million, will fuel the growth of its existing leagues, Overtime Elite (OTE) and OT7, and support expansion into new content, e-commerce, Web 3.0 initiatives, and the creation of additional disruptive sports leagues. Overtime CEO Dan Porter emphasized the validation of their innovative sports IP and the potential for future league development.

title: Walmart Acquires Volt Systems To Advance Omnichannel Capabilities
summary: Walmart has acquired Volt Systems, a technology company specializing in providing suppliers with enhanced on-demand visibility into merchandising resources. This acquisition aims to strengthen Walmart's omnichannel shopping experience by optimizing product assortment and reducing out-of-stocks through store-level data and actionable analytics. The move highlights Walmart's continued investment in technology to anticipate customer demand and integrate various initiatives across its enterprise.

title: Tech, Cyber Companies Launch Security Standard to Monitor Hacking Attempts
summary: A consortium of 18 technology and cybersecurity companies, including AWS, Splunk, and IBM, have launched a new common data standard called the Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF). This initiative aims to standardize the sharing of cybersecurity information, addressing a long-standing issue for corporate security chiefs regarding the lack of integration between various proprietary cyber products. The goal is to improve the assessment of hacking threats by creating a unified approach to data.

title: Spotify starts selling live music tickets to fans directly
summary: Spotify has launched a new website to sell live concert tickets directly to fans, moving away from exclusively redirecting users to third-party partners like Ticketmaster. This new platform, currently in a testing phase, lists upcoming gigs primarily in the U.S. and allows users to purchase tickets with a Spotify account, aiming to improve event discovery and potentially generate revenue beyond streaming. The company has not yet disclosed details on booking fees or how this new initiative integrates with its existing live events features.

title: Grove, Inc. Announces Name Change to Upexi, Inc.
summary: Grove, Inc. has officially changed its name to Upexi, Inc., reflecting its evolution beyond a hemp company into a broader consumer brands, SaaS programmatic advertising, and reseller business. The company plans to focus on direct-to-consumer markets, leveraging an advertising platform for customer data, and expanding through organic growth and acquisitions to create a strong ecosystem for brand development.

title: Megazone Cloud receives $343 mn from MBK, IMM PE in Series C funding
summary: Megazone Cloud, South Korea’s largest managed cloud service provider, has closed its Series C funding round with 450 billion won ($343 million) from MBK Partners and IMM Private Equity. This investment, combined with an earlier one from KT Corp., brings the company's valuation to 2.4 trillion won, making it a unicorn. Megazone Cloud is also preparing for an IPO by the end of 2023.

title: FedEx, Berkshire Grey Expand Robotics Deal
summary: FedEx and Berkshire Grey have expanded their strategic relationship, focusing on AI-enabled robotic solutions to enhance FedEx's package handling operations globally. The agreement includes new development activities and a master system purchase agreement to streamline procurement of Berkshire Grey solutions. Additionally, Berkshire Grey granted FedEx a warrant to purchase common stock, vesting based on FedEx's investment in robotics and services.

title: Amazon is partnering with GE and GE Appliances to stop counterfeiters
summary: Amazon, alongside General Electric (GE) and GE Appliances, has filed a joint lawsuit against 16 defendants for selling counterfeit GE-branded water filters. This action is part of Amazon's broader effort to protect customers and brands from counterfeiting through proactive controls, brand protection tools, and holding fraudsters accountable. GE Appliances emphasized the risks associated with fake filters, which fail to provide adequate filtration and can damage appliances.

title: How Microsoft secures its spot among the world's most valuable brands
summary: Microsoft has become one of the world's most valuable brands, with its brand value reaching $661 billion in 2022, securing the number four spot in Kantar BrandZ Most Valuable Global Brands. The company's success is attributed to its meaningful, different, and salient offerings, including superior cloud, software, and hardware products, as well as its commitment to sustainability. Under CEO Satya Nadella, Microsoft has focused on specific market segments, leading to a tenfold increase in brand value and solidifying its position as the world's most valuable business services brand, further boosted by the continued digital transformation and remote work trends.

title: The Forrester Wave™: Anti-Money Laundering Solutions, Q2 2025
summary: SAS has been recognized as a leader in The Forrester Wave™: Anti-Money Laundering Solutions, Q2 2025 report. Forrester notes that SAS's recent acquisition of Hazy synthetic data software is expected to enhance its Financial Crime Compliance portfolio, especially with large data models and Generative AI. The report highlights SAS's AML solution as suitable for enterprises with existing SAS and data science skills, emphasizing its strong framework for quantifying ROI.

title: Tony the Tiger® Tackles Twitch and Becomes the First-Ever Brand Mascot Working with Twitch to Transform into an Interactive VTuber
summary: Kellogg's Frosted Flakes and Tony the Tiger are collaborating with Twitch to transform Tony the Tiger into an interactive VTuber for a livestreamed gaming event. This marks the first time a brand mascot will engage with Twitch in this capacity, with Tony competing against popular streamers in a battle royale game. The event aims to connect with new audiences and deepen engagement with fans through an innovative gaming experience.

title: Walmart Reaches Video-Streaming Deal to Offer Paramount+ to Members
summary: Walmart Inc. has partnered with Paramount Global to offer its Paramount+ streaming service to subscribers of Walmart's membership program, Walmart+. This move is part of Walmart's strategy to attract more members and compete with Amazon.com Inc.'s successful Prime membership program. The deal makes an ad-supported version of Paramount+ available as a perk for Walmart+ subscribers.

title: Walmart partners with Paramount+ to better compete with Amazon Prime
summary: Walmart announced a deal with Paramount Global to include the Paramount+ streaming service as a perk for its Walmart+ shipping subscription members, aiming to better compete with Amazon Prime. This addition will not change the Walmart+ annual fee of $98 or monthly fee of $12.95, and comes as many other streaming services are increasing prices. The move helps Walmart enhance its membership offering, which also includes free shipping and gasoline discounts.

title: Future Farm launches at Amazon Fresh and Sprouts
summary: Future Farm, a leading Brazilian plant-based meat company, has expanded its U.S. distribution by launching products nationwide on Amazon Fresh and making its retail store debut at Sprouts Farmers Market in Southern California. This move follows initial e-commerce sales in July 2021 and aligns with the company's mission to democratize plant-based food and accelerate international growth. The company also plans to introduce new products like Future Chick'n and Future Tuna in the U.S. and expand into plant-based drinks and dairy.

title: Google Strikes Back at Sonos; SmartSpeaker War Gets Ugly
summary: Google has sued Sonos for patent infringement, escalating an ongoing battle over smart home audio technology. This comes after Sonos previously won a ruling against Google regarding similar claims. The conflict highlights broader issues of antitrust concerns and data privacy in the smart speaker market, with Sonos launching its own privacy-focused voice assistant.

title: Worksport Launches All-New E-Commerce Online Platform
summary: Worksport Ltd. has launched a new e-Commerce platform to sell its proprietary truck bed tonneau covers, including the SC3, SC3 Pro, and SC4. The platform, shopworksport.com, will later feature its hard cover TC3 and flagship products SOLIS (solar-integrated tonneau cover) and COR (portable energy storage system). This initiative aims to streamline production and sales, with products also available on Walmart, Amazon, and eBay.

title: Amazon was Roomba marketer's biggest customer long before $1.7 billion deal
summary: Amazon was the largest customer for Roomba's marketer well in advance of its $1.7 billion acquisition deal. This indicates a pre-existing significant business relationship between the two companies.

title: BigCommerce Named as a Challenger in 2022 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Digital Commerce Platforms for Third Consecutive Year
summary: BigCommerce has been recognized as a Challenger in the 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Digital Commerce for the third consecutive year. This recognition highlights BigCommerce's ability to provide flexible e-commerce solutions for enterprise businesses, supported by recent acquisitions and global expansion. The evaluation was based on the company's Completeness of Vision and Ability to Execute in providing core technology for interactive digital commerce experiences.

title: Capital Budgets Fall to 13% of IT Spending
summary: Capital budgets now constitute only 13% of IT spending in North American companies, a significant drop from 24% in 2013, as businesses shift away from on-premises infrastructure towards public cloud and subscription-based applications. While total IT spending is projected to increase, the allocation is largely towards operational expenditures like cloud infrastructure and applications rather than long-term capital investments. This shift brings flexibility but also risks of being locked into difficult-to-negotiate operational contracts.

title: Kohl’s adding in-store Sephora shops at all locations
summary: Kohl's is significantly expanding its partnership with Sephora, planning to open Sephora shop-in-shops in all 1,100-plus Kohl's stores nationwide. This expansion, which projects to achieve $2 billion in annual sales by 2025, aims to attract new, younger, and more diverse customers, with current stores already showing a sales lift and increased customer visits. The initiative also includes new joint offerings like Sephora gift card redemption at Kohl's and a planned cross-company buy online, pick up in-store (BOPIS) service.

title: Startup Digs Into Public Filings With GPU-Driven Machine Learning to Serve Up Alternative Financial Data Services
summary: Intrinio, a startup based in St. Petersburg, Fla., uses GPU-driven machine learning to parse publicly available financial data, offering an alternative to traditional, bundled financial data products. Co-founded by Rachel Carpenter and Joseph French, Intrinio provides à la carte subscription services for equities, options, estimates, ETFs, and ESG data, making it more affordable and accessible for fintech innovators and startups. The company's technology significantly reduces errors and streamlines data cleansing and standardization, allowing clients like Robinhood, FTX, and Aiera to integrate high-quality financial data into their platforms.

title: Report: Qualcomm plans to return to the server chip market
summary: Qualcomm Inc. is reportedly planning to re-enter the server chip market four years after exiting it, seeking customers for a new server processor. This new processor is based on technology acquired from Nuvia Inc. for $1.4 billion and is being evaluated by Amazon Web Services Inc. The move aligns with Qualcomm's strategy to expand beyond mobile and boost revenue, potentially increasing competition for Intel Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.

title: R|T: The Retail Times – Groupon to focus on ‘mission critical activities’ following staff cuts
summary: Groupon has cut over 500 staff and plans to focus solely on "mission-critical activities" due to underperforming business. This move is intended to improve its trajectory and generate positive cash flow by the end of 2022, following similar workforce reductions by other tech giants like Alibaba and Amazon. The article also provides updates on various other tech companies, including funding rounds, layoffs, and strategic partnerships.

title: Amazon (AWS) and Microsoft Data Centers in Virginia
summary: This article details the extensive presence of Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft data centers across Virginia, highlighting locations in both Northern Virginia and emerging areas like Boydton. It outlines specific data center sites, their sizes, and ongoing development plans for both companies, emphasizing their investments and strategic growth in the region. The report also covers their respective cloud regions, availability zones, and cloud on-ramps to support demand for compute, storage, and database capabilities.

title: Qualcomm planning return to server market with new chip - Bloomberg News
summary: Qualcomm Inc. is reportedly planning a return to the server market with a new chip, aiming to reduce its dependence on smartphones. The company is seeking customers for a product based on its Nuvia Inc. acquisition, with Amazon Web Services (AWS) agreeing to evaluate the offerings. This move comes as Qualcomm faces a slowdown in smartphone demand, impacting its core handset chip business.

title: How Amazon’s DSP program has created $26 billion in revenue for owners
summary: Amazon's Delivery Service Partner (DSP) program has generated over $26 billion in revenue for small businesses since its inception four years ago. The program has enabled nearly 3,000 entrepreneurs to scale their operations, employ 275,000 drivers, and deliver over 10 million packages daily across more than 14 countries. Amazon continues to expand the DSP program, focusing on supporting underrepresented entrepreneurs and developing sustainable, carbon-neutral delivery methods such as electric vehicles.

title: ANA Group drones to fly medical & daily supplies to remote regions around the world
summary: ANA Group is developing a drone delivery service to provide medical supplies and daily necessities to remote areas, leveraging its airline expertise. The initiative aims to address social issues in Japan by cutting down delivery times significantly and reducing costs through automation. ANA also plans to expand these drone operations internationally, particularly for medical infrastructure in developing nations, despite a previous project in Zambia being canceled due to the pandemic.

title: Paramount renews U.S. rights to Champions League valued at $1.5 billion
summary: Paramount Global has renewed its U.S. media rights for the UEFA Champions League in a six-year deal valued at over $1.5 billion, more than double its previous contract. This agreement, running from 2024 to 2030, reflects the growing popularity of football in the U.S. and further emphasizes the rising cost of sports broadcasting rights. Paramount will pay approximately $250 million annually to air the matches on its CBS network and Paramount+ streaming service.

title: Aflac virtualizes the customer enrollment experience
summary: Aflac successfully virtualized its customer enrollment experience during the pandemic to support its independent agents, who were facing significant business risks due to social distancing. By combining existing technologies and building a new enrollment platform on AWS, Aflac enabled agents to conduct virtual meetings, co-browse with clients, and process policy purchases more efficiently. This digital transformation, which included the development of microsites and a "bionic" agent approach, earned Aflac a CIO 100 Award and lays the groundwork for a full migration to the cloud and further intelligent automation.

title: Amazfit、コンパクトでパワフルな新モデルのスマートウォッチ 「Amazfit GTS 4 Mini」を発売
summary: Zepp Health Corporationの独自ブランド「Amazfit」が、コンパクトでパワフルなスマートウォッチ「Amazfit GTS 4 Mini」を発売しました。このモデルは、薄型軽量デザインと1.65型HD AMOLEDディスプレイを特徴とし、最大45日間のバッテリー寿命、5種類の衛星測位システム対応、120種類以上のスポーツモードを搭載しています。価格は1万6800円で、公式オンラインストアなどで販売されます。

title: Amazfit、新スマートウォッチ「GTS 4 Mini」。薄型軽量／15日間バッテリー
summary: Zepp Health CorporationがAmazfitブランドから新スマートウォッチ「Amazfit GTS 4 Mini」を発売しました。このスマートウォッチは、31.2gの薄型軽量デザインと最大15日間のロングバッテリーライフが特徴で、価格は16,800円（税込）です。直販ストアや主要ECサイトでのオンライン限定販売となります。

title: Amazon’s Signify Health Interest Another Indicator Of At-Home Care Capabilities Buildout
summary: Amazon is reportedly interested in acquiring Signify Health, a value-based care platform with significant home-based care capabilities, just a month after purchasing One Medical. This move signals Amazon's continued expansion into the healthcare sector, particularly strengthening its at-home care offerings. The acquisition could position Amazon to better appeal to payers by leveraging Signify's in-home assessments and integration with the healthcare ecosystem.

title: CVS, Amazon, UnitedHealth are among bidders for Signify, Bloomberg reports
summary: CVS Health, Amazon, and UnitedHealth Group are among the companies bidding to acquire home health firm Signify Health, according to Bloomberg News. UnitedHealth has reportedly submitted the highest offer at $30 per share, with Amazon close behind. The potential acquisition aligns with a trend of companies like CVS and Amazon expanding their healthcare services, though antitrust concerns remain a factor in such deals.

title: Target announces opening date for Scotts Valley store
summary: Target Corporation has announced that its new 55,000-square-foot Scotts Valley store will open on September 25, 2022. This opening comes after Target experienced a significant profit drop nationally but also follows a period of growth that allowed them to acquire former Kmart locations. The new store is expected to bring major changes to the Scotts Valley Square Shopping Center, with some existing small businesses, like Earthwise Pet Supply, facing displacement due to rent increases by the property manager.

title: Signify Health shares jump as Amazon, UnitedHealth reportedly among bidders for takeover deal
summary: Signify Health's shares surged after reports indicated Amazon and UnitedHealth Group are among the bidders for the home health technology and services provider in a deal potentially exceeding $8 billion. This comes as Signify focuses on its home and community services segment and other major players like CVS, Walgreens, and Walmart intensify their efforts in the healthcare market. A potential acquisition by Amazon would mark its second major healthcare deal in 2022, while for UnitedHealth, it aligns with its vertical integration strategy.

title: Ohio searching for 7,000 construction workers to build Intel chip plants
summary: Ohio faces a significant challenge in finding 7,000 construction workers for Intel's new $20 billion semiconductor manufacturing operation, a project that is among the state's largest ever. This shortage is exacerbated by an already thriving construction market and a national deficit of skilled tradespeople. State officials and Intel are addressing this through educational funding, training programs, and the high wages expected for these jobs, acknowledging that the project's scale will likely attract new workers and potentially shift some from residential construction, which could impact housing availability.

title: You may be eligible for part of a $190M Capital One settlement: How to know
summary: Capital One has reached a $190 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit following a 2019 data breach that affected over 100 million customer accounts. Eligible individuals, who were notified by Capital One, can claim reimbursement for lost time and out-of-pocket expenses related to the breach, or enroll in identity defense services. The deadline to file a claim has been extended to September 30, 2022, with a final approval hearing for the settlement scheduled for September 8.

title: A Tax Credit Was Meant to Help Marginalized Workers Get Permanent Jobs. Instead It’s Subsidizing Temp Work.
summary: The Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC), designed to incentivize permanent employment for marginalized workers, is instead largely subsidizing short-term temp jobs. ProPublica's analysis shows a significant portion of WOTC benefits go to temp agencies, many with histories of labor violations, without leading to long-term employment for individuals like formerly incarcerated DeMond Bush and Courtney Decker. Critics argue the program is failing its original intent, benefiting businesses with high turnover while providing little lasting impact for vulnerable workers.

title: Warner Music’s HipHopDX Asia Launches ‘The Regionals’ – The First-Ever Pan-Asia Cypher Series
summary: Warner Music's HipHopDX Asia has launched 'The Regionals,' a pioneering pan-Asia rap cypher series designed to globalize Asian hip-hop music. This initiative brings together top emcees from various Eastern markets and pairs them with acclaimed Western hip-hop producers like !llmind, Hit-Boy, and 9th Wonder. The project aims to showcase diverse talent, connect global hip-hop communities, and promote Asian hip-hop culture worldwide, with the first cyphers scheduled for release in September.

title: Convera CEO revamps former Western Union biz
summary: Patrick Gauthier, former head of Amazon Pay, is leading the rebranding and modernization of Convera, the former B2B cross-border payments unit of Western Union. Acquired by Goldfinch Partners and The Baupost Group for $910 million, Convera aims to assist its 30,000 corporate clients in 200 countries in navigating increased currency volatility through a cloud-based platform and tailored risk management solutions. Gauthier plans to enhance customer engagement and build the Convera brand distinct from Western Union's consumer association.

title: These Wide-Moat Stocks Are Gaining Ground
summary: Quality stocks with wide economic moats, including Microsoft and Amazon, have outperformed since the bear market low in June, despite still being undervalued. While narrow-moat stocks have seen stronger recent gains due to market-cap weighting of companies like Apple and Tesla, wide-moat companies are better positioned to handle inflation due to their pricing power. Overall, Morningstar analysts consider wide-moat stocks to be deeply undervalued compared to overpriced narrow-moat stocks.

title: Tech Moves: Opendoor hires Seattle tech vet as CTO; Vacasa names CEO; ex-Blue Origin comms chief lands at Clorox
summary: Opendoor has appointed Raji Subramanian, a former Yahoo and Amazon engineering leader and co-founder of Pro.com, as its new Chief Technology Officer. Meanwhile, vacation rental company Vacasa named Rob Greyber, previously president of Egencia, as its CEO. Additionally, Linda Mills, a communications veteran from Blue Origin, joined Clorox as Chief Communications Officer.

title: Changes in consumer behaviour mean new opportunities for retailers in cross-border e-commerce
summary: The e-commerce sector is experiencing remarkable growth, with cross-border transactions playing an increasingly significant role, projected to exceed US$7.4 trillion by 2025. This shift is driven by changing consumer behaviors, expedited by the pandemic, leading more shoppers to purchase from international merchants. Retailers can leverage this trend to expand their customer base globally, despite challenges like supply chain issues and inflation, by customizing experiences and offering diverse payment options.

title: Making AI Run At Any Scale But Not At All Costs
summary: This article discusses the challenges and solutions for scaling AI applications, highlighting how companies like HPE and Lenovo are developing accessible AI products. It focuses on Anyscale, a company founded by UC Berkeley researchers, which commercializes the open-source Ray framework to simplify distributed AI computing and make it easier for enterprises to develop and deploy AI models without extensive infrastructure expertise.

title: Pleb Miner Month Celebrates The Rise Of Home Bitcoin Miners
summary: Pleb Miner Month, organized by Jon and Sarah DiGiacomo and MaxBitBuyBit, will highlight small-scale and home Bitcoin miners throughout September. The initiative aims to decentralize Bitcoin mining discussions, moving away from large corporate events, and will feature interviews, educational content, and raffles of mining equipment. The month-long celebration emphasizes that Bitcoin mining began at home with Satoshi Nakamoto and that individual "pleb miners" are crucial for securing the network's decentralization and upholding its foundational principles.

title: Amazon says it will shut down Amazon Care, its primary and urgent health care business.
summary: Amazon announced it is shutting down its primary and urgent health care service, Amazon Care, by the end of the year. This decision comes shortly after the company revealed plans to acquire One Medical, a larger health care competitor, for $3.9 billion. Amazon Care, which began in 2019 for Amazon employees and later expanded, struggled to attract large enterprise customers, leading to the conclusion that it was not a complete enough offering for long-term viability.

title: Target Announces Opening Date for Scotts Valley Store
summary: Target Corporation has announced that its Scotts Valley store, located at 270 Mt. Hermon Road, is scheduled to open on September 25th. This new 55,000-square-foot store follows the company's strategy of acquiring former Kmart locations. While bringing a major retailer to the area, the new development has also led to increased rents and closures for several small businesses in the Scotts Valley Square Shopping Center.

title: Rackspace’s intention not to sell leaves Wall Street wary
summary: Rackspace Technology Inc. has decided against selling the company and will instead pursue a restructuring plan, disappointing some Wall Street analysts. The cloud-computing services provider, the largest tech company in San Antonio, will realign into separate business units for private and public clouds. This decision led to a significant drop in share prices as analysts downgraded the stock, expressing skepticism about the standalone strategy's ability to create shareholder value quickly.

title: Another option for fiber-optic internet launching in Phoenix metro
summary: Lumen Technologies is launching its fiber-optic internet service, Quantum Fiber, in the Phoenix metropolitan area. This subscription-based service will be rolled out to several cities across the Valley, expanding internet options for residents.

title: As big-box stores drop prices, how have spending trends changed at Walmart and Target?
summary: This article analyzes spending trends at Target and Walmart in 2022, revealing that Walmart's average transaction values generally increased year-over-year, while Target's slightly decreased. It also highlights the sustained elevation of online sales share for both retailers compared to pre-pandemic levels and notes a shift in consumer spending towards groceries, especially at Walmart, amidst inflationary pressures.

title: Amazon Plans to Shut Amazon Care Service Amid One Medical Overlap (AMZN)
summary: Amazon.com Inc. is shutting down its Amazon Care primary care and telehealth service by the end of the year. This decision comes shortly after the company announced its intention to acquire the One Medical chain of clinics, indicating an overlap in services. Senior Vice President Neil Lindsay communicated the closure to the Amazon health care team, stating that Amazon Care was not a "complete enough offering."

title: Pick n Pay Selects AWS as Its Strategic Cloud Provider
summary: Pick n Pay, a leading retail business in South African and other African countries, has migrated its entire on-premises IT infrastructure to Amazon Web Services (AWS) with the help of Lemongrass Consulting. This move positions Pick n Pay as the first sub-Saharan African retailer to complete an all-in migration to AWS. The migration aims to streamline operations, modernize the supply chain, develop new digital customer experiences, and enable data-driven decisions for better efficiency and value.

title: PR News | Ex-Bush II Aide Lands at Truist Financial - Thu., Aug. 25, 2022
summary: Scott Stanzel, a former communications official in the George W. Bush White House, has been appointed as EVP and CCO of Truist Financial Corporation, effective October 1. He will lead corporate communications from the Charlotte, NC headquarters, overseeing internal and external communications. Stanzel brings a wealth of experience from previous roles at Capital One, Amazon, and Microsoft.

title: Compass CTO is out; brokerage laying off tech employees
summary: Compass has parted ways with its Chief Technology Officer, Joseph Sirosh, and is laying off a "small" number of tech employees and recruiters as part of a $320 million cost-cutting initiative. This move signifies a shift for Compass, emphasizing its role as a residential brokerage rather than solely a technology company, despite having invested heavily in its tech platform. Kendra Shimmell and Shay Artzi will take over some of Sirosh's duties, though his CTO position will not be directly replaced.

title: Amazon strikes green hydrogen deal with fuel cell maker Plug Power, sending shares up
summary: Amazon has struck a deal with fuel cell maker Plug Power to power some of its operations with green hydrogen, causing Plug Power's stock to surge 9%, while Amazon's shares also closed up 2.6%. Under the agreement, Plug will provide 10,950 tons of green hydrogen annually for Amazon's transportation and building operations starting in 2025. This deal includes a warrant for Amazon to purchase up to 16 million shares of Plug Power, contingent on Amazon spending $2.1 billion on Plug products over seven years.

title: Amazon mothballing virtual health care service after admitting, ‘It is not a complete enough offering’
summary: Amazon is discontinuing its telehealth service, Amazon Care, by December 31, 2022, citing that it is "not a complete enough offering" for large enterprise customers. This decision comes despite the company's broader expansion into healthcare through acquisitions like PillPack and One Medical, and marks a potential setback for the telehealth industry as demand has reportedly declined. However, Amazon's other healthcare initiatives remain unaffected.

title: Lawsuit filed against Block
summary: Block and its Cash App Investing product are facing a potential class-action lawsuit following a December 2021 data breach that affected 8.2 million investor accounts. The lawsuit alleges Block failed to adequately protect customer data and delayed notifying affected individuals, leading to charges and withdrawal attempts on accounts. Plaintiffs Michelle Salinas and Raymel Washington are seeking class-action status, claiming heightened risk of identity theft and fraud due to the breach.

title: Peloton to sell its bikes on Amazon in bid to reverse slump
summary: Peloton will now sell its high-end exercise bikes and other equipment on Amazon in the U.S., marking its first partnership with an external retailer. This move aims to boost the fitness company's sales, which have declined since pandemic lockdowns eased. Despite this effort, Peloton's shares are still significantly down over the past year.

title: Amazon adopts green hydrogen to help decarbonize its operations
summary: Amazon has signed a significant agreement with Plug Power to procure 10,950 tons of green hydrogen annually starting in 2025, aiming to decarbonize its transportation and building operations. This initiative is part of Amazon's commitment to be net-zero carbon by 2040 and will provide enough power for 30,000 forklifts or 800 heavy-duty trucks. The company is also investing in electrolyzer technology through its Climate Pledge Fund to further scale green hydrogen production and adoption.

title: UnitedHealth CFO is added to class-action lawsuit over 401(k) plan
summary: UnitedHealth Group Inc.'s CFO, John Rex, has been added to a 2021 class-action lawsuit concerning the company's 401(k) plans. This amendment implicates a key financial officer in the ongoing legal challenge against the healthcare giant.

title: Tesla shares close lower after 3-1 stock split
summary: Tesla's shares closed 2% lower after its three-for-one stock split took effect, aimed at attracting retail investors. The stock opened at $302 and closed at $296.07 after previously closing at $891.29 before the split. This marks Tesla's second stock split in two years, a strategy adopted by high-growth companies to make shares more affordable for individual investors.

title: Musk's SpaceX and T-Mobile plan to connect mobile phones to satellites, boost cell coverage
summary: T-Mobile US Inc. announced a partnership with Elon Musk's SpaceX Starlink to provide satellite-based mobile network access to users in remote areas of the United States. This service will allow mobile phones to connect directly to Starlink satellites, initially supporting texting services in a beta phase, thereby extending coverage beyond traditional cell towers. The plan aims to use T-Mobile's mid-band spectrum with SpaceX's next-generation satellites, eliminating the need for new phones for existing T-Mobile customers.

title: EA Pares Gains After Retraction of Report on Amazon Prepping Bid
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) shares surged after a report claimed Amazon was preparing a takeover bid, but the gains were pared following the retraction of the report by USA Today. The initial news sent EA's stock up by as much as 16%, however, the report was later discredited due to unreliable sourcing. Bloomberg's David Faber also cast doubt on the possibility of an imminent deal.

title: Focus: FedEx missteps fuel contractor's crusade as pandemic delivery boom fades
summary: FedEx faces increasing pressure from Spencer Patton, one of its largest delivery contractors, to boost compensation. Patton argues that many contractors are at risk of financial collapse due to FedEx's actions and an inflationary economy, exacerbated by inaccurate holiday volume forecasts and uncompensated Sunday deliveries. FedEx, meanwhile, has sued Patton for disparaging its business, as the dispute threatens to disrupt crucial holiday shipping.

title: Amazon not expected to bid for Electronic Arts, says CNBC
summary: CNBC reported that Amazon.com Inc is not expected to bid for Electronic Arts Inc, refuting an earlier report about a potential takeover. This news caused EA's stock to fluctuate, initially jumping 15% on the acquisition rumor before settling to a 4% gain. Amazon has recently been active in acquisitions, diversifying its business, while analysts see EA as an attractive target due to its strong licenses and metaverse potential, despite a struggling global gaming industry.

title: DXL’s Shift Away from Deep Discounts is Working
summary: Destination XL Group (DXL) is successfully moving away from deep discounting, as evidenced by its Q2 2022 net sales of $144.6 million and increased sales guidance for fiscal 2022. The "big and tall" men’s wear retailer has reduced clearance inventory and lowered maximum discount levels, contributing to improved gross margins and higher dollars per transaction. DXL plans to open up to 50 net new stores in the next three to five years, indicating confidence in its current strategy and market position.

title: Amazon’s rumored purchase of Orlando's EA doesn’t materialize
summary: Rumors about Amazon acquiring Electronic Arts (EA) have not materialized. EA, which employs over 1,000 people in Central Florida, had relocated its office from Maitland to a new 175,000-square-foot facility in downtown Orlando's Creative Village district. The article highlights that these acquisition rumors did not lead to an actual purchase.

title: Amazon announces 750-job sortation center in Liberty Commerce Center
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has opened a new 517,000-square-foot sortation center in the Liberty Commerce Center. This facility is Amazon's 11th announced and 12th known location in the Kansas City metro area. The new center is expected to create 750 jobs.

title: AI hiring bias: Everything you need to know
summary: AI hiring tools can significantly streamline the recruitment process but carry a substantial risk of amplifying existing biases against protected groups if not properly managed. The article discusses how AI bias can manifest in various stages of hiring, from sourcing to offer, and outlines four key strategies to mitigate these biases, including keeping humans in the loop, avoiding biased data elements, emphasizing protected groups, and quantifying success objectively. It also touches on government and legal concerns regarding AI-driven hiring practices.

title: With Spoken, two retail newbies are exposing white labeling across furniture retailers
summary: Spoken, founded by Dane Hurtubise and Geoff Abraham, is a new website that helps consumers identify white-labeled furniture products sold under different brand names and prices by various retailers. The platform "codebreaks" popular retailers, revealing that identical items can often be found much cheaper elsewhere. Spoken has gained significant traction through viral social media moments, attracting over 100,000 monthly users by empowering consumers with transparent pricing information.

title: What you need to know about the new ADS development in Hilliard
summary: Advanced Drainage Systems (ADS) is set to construct a new $65-million, 110,000-square-foot office, warehouse, and laboratory facility on 17 acres in Hilliard, solidifying its commitment to the city. This expansion will consolidate engineering and technology operations, creating 200 new jobs and retaining 322 existing ones in Ohio, bringing $20 million in new payroll. The facility will enhance the company's leading role in plastic recycling and stormwater management, utilizing advanced labs for product development.

title: Movie tickets to cost just $3 on 'National Cinema Day' across U.S.
summary: Movie tickets will be available for just $3 across most cinemas in the United States on September 3, as part of 'National Cinema Day'. This initiative, spearheaded by The Cinema Foundation, aims to encourage moviegoers back to theaters after a significant lull during the pandemic. Over 3,000 theaters and 30,000 screens will participate, offering tickets at the discounted price, excluding tax, for all formats and show times.

title: Amazon Seller Packable to Shut Down in Bankruptcy After SPAC Deal Sinks
summary: Packable Holdings LLC, an Amazon third-party seller of health and beauty products, is filing for bankruptcy protection after a failed SPAC merger prevented it from going public. The company, once valued at over $1 billion with nearly 1,300 employees, has already laid off 138 workers and now enters bankruptcy with 372. Private-equity firm Carlyle Group holds a 26% stake in the e-commerce platform.

title: How Royal Caribbean set up a seafaring cloud strategy
summary: Royal Caribbean Group has adopted a multicloud strategy to manage the complex IT needs of its cruise ship fleet, leveraging Google Cloud, AWS, and Microsoft Azure for different workloads. This approach helps address the unique challenges of seafaring operations, such as unreliable satellite connectivity and the need for robust hybrid solutions. The company emphasizes the importance of balancing internal expertise with external partners and carefully considering cost and talent access in its vendor selection process.

title: Thermo Fisher Opens $105M Nashville-Area Tech Plant
summary: Thermo Fisher Scientific Inc. has opened a new 400,000-square-foot bioprocessing production plant in Lebanon, Tenn., near Nashville. This $105 million facility, developed by Panattoni within Speedway Industrial Park, is the company's largest single-use manufacturing site and is expected to create up to 1,400 jobs. The development highlights Nashville's growing prominence as a life science hub, supported by institutions like Vanderbilt University Medical Center.

title: 40 Under 40 in Home Entertainment, Class of 2022
summary: Media Play News announced its fifth annual "40 Under 40 in Home Entertainment" list, recognizing rising stars and young executives navigating the evolving home entertainment landscape. This year's honorees are playing crucial roles in an era dominated by various video-on-demand models and increasing reliance on data analysis. They are tasked with balancing current business needs with future advancements in the industry.

title: Amazon Fresh to open in revamped Montgomery County shopping center, documents show
summary: Amazon Fresh is planning to open a new grocery store in a redeveloped shopping center in Montgomery County, Pennsylvania. This location marks another expansion for Amazon Fresh in the Philadelphia region, following other announced area stores. The information was revealed through official documents.

title: Netflix Hires Snap Execs Jeremi Gorman And Peter Naylor To Lead Its Push Into Advertising
summary: Netflix has hired Jeremi Gorman and Peter Naylor, both formerly of Snap Inc., to lead its new ad-supported subscription tier. Gorman will serve as President, Worldwide Advertising, and Naylor as VP Advertising Sales. This move comes as Netflix prepares for a significant business pivot in response to increased competition and subscriber challenges.

title: Announcing VMware Cloud on AWS integration with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP
summary: NetApp announces the integration of VMware Cloud on AWS with Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP, offering an integrated, certified, and supported external NFS datastore. This solution allows for independent scaling of compute and storage in the cloud, leading to significant cost savings (up to 25-50% TCO reduction) and simplified data management for data-intensive VMware workloads. The partnership leverages 20 years of collaboration between NetApp and VMware to reduce barriers to cloud migration.

title: Netflix hires two top ad executives from Snap
summary: Netflix has hired Jeremi Gorman as president of worldwide advertising and Peter Naylor as vice president of ad sales, both formerly top executives at Snap Inc. These strategic hires signal Netflix's serious commitment to launching an ad-supported streaming service next year, leveraging Gorman and Naylor's strong relationships with brands and advertisers from their previous roles at Snap and Amazon.

title: Garmin Vivosmart 5 vs Fitbit Charge 5 vs Inspire 3: Fitness band face-off
summary: This article compares three popular fitness trackers: Garmin Vivosmart 5, Fitbit Charge 5, and Fitbit Inspire 3, examining their design, hardware, and health tracking capabilities. It highlights that while smartwatches are popular, fitness bands offer similar metrics in a less bulky design with better battery life, making them a cost-effective alternative. The comparison concludes that the Fitbit Charge 5 generally offers more advanced features like built-in GPS, ECG, and a superior AMOLED display for the same price as the Vivosmart 5, while the Inspire 3 is a discreet, budget-friendly option.

title: Songwriters and Music Publishers to Be Paid More by Streaming Services
summary: Music publishers and streaming services have reached an agreement to increase the rates paid to songwriters for their music played on digital platforms like Spotify. This deal, struck between the National Music Publishers Association and the Digital Media Association, means publishers will receive up to 15.35% of music streamers’ revenue, which will be phased in over a five-year period. The agreement was finalized just before a trial was set to begin in front of the Copyright Royalty Board.

title: Xperi Announces TiVo OS Smart TV Launch, First OEM Customer
summary: Xperi has officially launched its TiVo OS independent media platform for smart TVs, announcing European TV producer Vestel as its first OEM customer. Vestel plans to ship the first "Powered by TiVo Smart TVs" in 2023 as part of a multi-year deal. Xperi aims to offer an independent, neutral platform distinguishing itself from "walled garden" smart TV operating systems, giving manufacturers more control and simplifying content discovery for consumers.

title: SpaceX, T-Mobile race to put an end to cell phone dead zones with help from outer space
summary: T-Mobile and SpaceX are collaborating to launch "Coverage Above and Beyond" service by late 2023, aiming to eliminate cellular dead zones across the continental U.S., Hawaii, parts of Alaska, and surrounding waters using SpaceX's Starlink satellites. The service will initially offer basic text and voice communications through existing smartphones, leveraging T-Mobile's 1900 MHz frequency. This initiative marks a significant step toward ubiquitous cellular coverage, with other companies like Apple and AST SpaceMobile also developing similar satellite-based phone connectivity solutions.
